purpose: Classify existing Rule Core discrete outputs relative to the declared authority, model, rule set, and provenance. An interval-backed boundary confirmation is stricter evidence of stability; neither mode claims absolute physical truth.

factFrame.statement: A FACT is the deterministic output produced by the declared provider/model and Rule Core for the requested input.
requiredIdentity: verified provider/source identity and applicable coverage
Rule Core identity and deterministic output
doesNotMean: stability across a decision boundary that the frozen guard does not clear

providerEquivalence.role: existing acceptance tolerance reference only; never an absolute truth bound

sign.confirmation: the complete longitude interval must remain in one half-open sign interval and farther than the guard from every real sign boundary; a central near_sign_boundary is not confirmed

aspect.guardDefinition: 1 arcminute from each inclusive max-orb acceptance boundary
aspect.confirmation: the complete angular-distance interval must remain inside exactly one aspect acceptance region, or outside every region, with the guard margin; selected identity and orbBoundaryStatus must agree

motion.confirmation: the complete speed interval must lie strictly above +epsilon for direct, strictly below -epsilon for retrograde, or wholly within [-epsilon,+epsilon] for stationary

aspectPhase.confirmation: phase is confirmed only when the signed-offset and relative-speed intervals yield one phase under the existing exact/indeterminate rules; missing angle speed remains unavailable

wholeSignHouse.confirmation: ASC sign and each requested body sign must be confirmed; no continuous cusp uncertainty is introduced

chartRuler.confirmation: ASC sign must be confirmed and both existing mappings must match the Rule Core output

distribution.confirmation: all required body signs must be confirmed; counts and tie state are then copied from the existing Rule Core without a tie-break

requiredPointEnvelope.longitude: absoluteErrorDegrees must be finite, non-negative, source-referenced, and no larger than the existing 0.01 degree acceptance ceiling
requiredPointEnvelope.speed: absoluteErrorDegreesPerDay must be finite, non-negative, source-referenced, and no larger than the existing 1e-7 degree/day acceptance ceiling when motion or phase is requested
requiredPointEnvelope.basis: source_relative_model_interval may describe a final-observable interval under the fixed source/model; it is not an absolute truth bound
requiredPointEnvelope.interval: the assessor treats the supplied central value ± bound as an interval; this interval is required only for interval-backed boundary confirmation and is never derived from a formal error, provider agreement, or time representation budget

dut1.meaning: reported internal formal precision, not a universal absolute truth bound
dut1.consumerAction: retain metadata; source-relative central FACTs keep the fixed provider identity, while interval-backed boundary confirmation must not infer a final bound from formal error alone

ttMinusUtc.source: frozen UTC-TAI history plus TT = TAI + 32.184 SI seconds
ttMinusUtc.meaning: piecewise source identity is fixed over the snapshot; binary64 arithmetic is a numerical property, not a final angular uncertainty bound
ttMinusUtc.consumerAction: require the bundle identity; an explicit final-observable interval is required only for interval-backed boundary confirmation

tdbMinusTt.meaning: model and time-representation quantities are kept separate; neither is silently converted into a longitude or speed bound
tdbMinusTt.consumerAction: retain the model identity; an independently justified final longitude/speed interval is required only for interval-backed boundary confirmation

providerEquivalence.meaning: raw/derived acceptance thresholds and empirical discrete agreement compare providers; they are not truth guarantees
providerEquivalence.consumerAction: never populate a missing uncertainty interval from equivalence output

uncertaintyModel.combinationPolicy: Only independently accepted component bounds may be conservatively summed and then recorded as an explicit source-relative final-observable interval. That interval is not a physical-truth bound. The assessor does not perform time-to-angle sensitivity propagation because the current contracts do not supply that derivative/error model.

resultRules.sign: a source-relative central sign remains a Rule Core FACT when its declared output is not near a sign boundary; interval-backed confirmation additionally requires the longitude interval to clear the sign guard, and missing/rejected interval is indeterminate or blocked
resultRules.motion: a source-relative central motion state remains a Rule Core FACT under the declared model; interval-backed confirmation requires the speed interval to stay on one side of or wholly inside the frozen epsilon bands, while missing speed remains unavailable
resultRules.aspectGeometry: a source-relative central aspect result remains a Rule Core FACT under the declared model; interval-backed confirmation additionally requires all candidate aspect regions to have a stable guarded match/no-match result, and any overlap or near-orb interval is indeterminate
resultRules.aspectPhase: a geometry-confirmed aspect may carry phaseStatus unavailable or indeterminate; that status must not be upgraded
resultRules.wholeSignHouse: confirmed only as a composition of confirmed ASC/body signs and matching whole_sign output
resultRules.chartRuler: confirmed only as the existing traditional/modern mapping of a confirmed ASC sign
resultRules.distribution: confirmed only for the complete required body set and matching counts/leaders/tie state; partial input is blocked

notes: A universal absolute physical-error bound is not a prerequisite for source-relative FACT consumption.
C04 formal error, provider-equivalence agreement, and the two-part-JD representation budget remain metadata or acceptance constraints and are not promoted to truth bounds.
The boundary assessor still returns indeterminate or blocked when a final-observable interval is missing, rejected, or does not clear the frozen guard.
